business_model.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business) and P3 (10-K Item 7 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Humana sells Medicare Advantage, stand-alone PDP, Medicare Supplement, state-based Medicaid and dual-eligible plans, specialty benefits (dental, vision, life, disability), military TRICARE administrative services, and a PBM business to Medicare beneficiaries, state Medicaid enrollees, military personnel, and employer groups, plus CenterWell pharmacy, primary care, and home solutions services.
quotes: Through our Humana insurance services, and our CenterWell health care services, we make it easier for the millions of people we serve to achieve their best health – delivering the care and service they need, when they need it.

The Insurance segment is comprised of insurance products serving Medicare and state-based contract beneficiaries, as well as individuals and employers. The segment also includes our Pharmacy Benefit Manager, or PBM, business.
The CenterWell segment includes our pharmacy solutions, primary care, and home solutions operations.

business_model.claim: Humana reports two segments: Insurance (Medicare, state-based contracts, specialty, military, PBM) and CenterWell (pharmacy solutions, primary care, home solutions), with the CEO as Chief Operating Decision Maker assessing performance by income from operations.
quotes: Our two reportable segments, Insurance and CenterWell, are based on a combination of the type of health plan customer and adjacent businesses centered on well-being solutions for our health plans and other customers.

Our Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Decision Maker, utilizes these segment groupings and results of each segment, measured by income (loss) from operations, to assess performance and allocate resources primarily during our annual budget process and periodic forecast updates.

business_model.claim: In 2025, 83% of Humana's total premiums and services revenue came from federal government contracts, with 14% specifically from Florida individual Medicare Advantage contracts covering approximately 1.0 million members.
quotes: During 2025, 83% of our total premiums and services revenue were derived from contracts with the federal government, including 14% derived from our individual Medicare Advantage contracts in Florida with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, or CMS, under which we provided health insurance coverage to approximately 1.0 million members as of December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: Operating costs (excluding depreciation and amortization) as a percentage of total revenues less investment income were 12.0% in 2025, up 20 basis points from 11.8% in 2024, driven by business mix shifts toward the higher-cost-ratio CenterWell segment, loss of MA membership, and value creation initiative charges.
quotes: The consolidated operating cost ratio increased 20 basis points from 11.8% in the 2024 period to 12.0% in the 2025 period primarily due to business mix changes, including within the CenterWell segment that runs a significantly higher operating cost ratio than the Insurance segment, the operating leverage impact associated with the loss of individual Medicare Advantage membership, as well as higher charges associated with the value creation plan.

business_model.claim: Humana recorded value creation initiative charges of $449 million in 2025, $281 million in 2024, and $436 million in 2023, primarily severance, asset impairments, and external consulting, as part of a multi-year transformation program to re-align its cost structure.
quotes: As a result of these initiatives, we recorded charges of $449 million, $281 million and $436 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, primarily within operating costs in the consolidated statements of income.

The value creation initiative charges primarily relate to $329 million, $25 million and $199 million in severance and other employee related charges in connection with workforce optimization in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, as well as $40 million, $256 million and $237 million in asset impairments in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.claim: The number of Humana's Medicare Advantage plans rated 4-star or higher significantly declined in 2025, and the company filed a lawsuit to vacate the 2025 Star Ratings; if unsuccessful, the decline will negatively impact 2026 quality bonus payments from CMS.

quotes: As a result of these initiatives, we recorded charges of $449 million, $281 million and $436 million in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, primarily within operating costs in the consolidated statements of income. We expect to incur additional charges over the course of the program.

The charges primarily relate to severance and associate exit costs, asset impairments, and external consulting expenses incurred to execute the program. We expect to incur additional charges over the course of the program.
